claims: C1 the example presents a root/developer conflict: a request that goes against the respect-creators section of the Model Spec
C2 the assistant must refuse to provide the full text of a copyrighted book even when a developer instruction says it can output any book at full length
C3 the good response refuses the full text and offers alternatives

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's text refers to the root authority level without defining it

concepts.name: developer_authority
concepts.gloss: D is an instruction issued at the developer authority level, assigned to Model Spec 'developer' sections and developer messages
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's text refers to the developer authority level without defining it

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: level H outranks level L in the authority hierarchy root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's text presupposes the ranking without stating it

concepts.name: instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction in the conversation or document
concepts.inference: the example involves a developer instruction and a root section instruction; a general instruction predicate is needed to refer to them

concepts.name: request
concepts.gloss: R is a request made by the user in the conversation
concepts.inference: the example involves a user request; a request predicate is needed to refer to it

concepts.name: copyrighted_book
concepts.gloss: B is a work protected by copyright law, such as a book, whose full text the user asks for
concepts.inference: the example concerns the full text of a copyrighted book; a book predicate is needed to refer to it

concepts.name: full_text_request
concepts.gloss: request R asks for the full text of book B
concepts.inference: the example's user request asks for the full text of a book; a relation between request and book is needed

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: request R conflicts with instruction I
concepts.inference: the example describes a request that goes against a section of the Model Spec; a conflict relation is needed

concepts.name: response
concepts.gloss: R is a response by the assistant
concepts.inference: the example compares two assistant responses; a response predicate is needed to refer to them

asserts.read_back: refusing to provide the full text of a copyrighted book is required when a request conflicts with the respect-creators section of the Model Spec, even if a developer instruction permits it
asserts.body: root_authority(I), developer_authority(D), authority_levels_hierarchy(root_level, developer_level), instruction(I), instruction(D), request(R), copyrighted_book(B), full_text_request(R, B), conflicts_with(R, I), conflicts_with(R, D), response(R)

closure.reason: the example's good response refuses the full text; the clause establishes a requirement to refuse, so silence about other acts does not permit them
